chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washa from Aban from Abu Baseer from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Had it not been that I would impose hardship upon my community, I would have delayed the Isha prayer until a third of the night.' And it is also reported (that he said): 'Until half the night.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time for delaying the Isha prayer according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of *Raf' al-Haraj* (removal of hardship) in Shia jurisprudence, illustrating how the Prophet's personal preference for extended night worship was balanced against communal ease. It underscores the distinction between the recommended *mustahabb* timing for Isha and the practical limits set to prevent burdening the Ummah, a key concept in Usul al-Fiqh. The narration reflects the Shia emphasis on the Prophet's role as a merciful leader who tailors religious obligations to the capacity of his followers.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhmmad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Had it not been grievous upon mysaww community, Isaww would have delayed Al-Isha (Salāt) up to a third of the night’. And it is reported as well (that hesaww said): ‘Up to half the night’.
en.sarwar: 13. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban from abu Basir from who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘If it was not because of al-Shafaq (bright redness), I would have delayed al-‘Isha’ Salah (prayer) up till passing of one-third of night.’” It is also narrated, “up till midnight.’”
